clue.text: Place on top of bird

parts.note: PL is the standard abbreviation for place, as in street addresses
over means on top of, as in a blanket over a bed

explanation.surface: An instruction to set something down on top of a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The plover is a wading shorebird of beaches and fields.

clue.text: Casual shoe, appropriate for layabout

explanation.surface: A slip-on shoe is said to suit an idle person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appropriate for' is a link joining the two definitions; the shoe sense and the idler sense share one spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A loafer is both a slip-on moccasin-style shoe and an idle person who lounges about.

clue.text: Give a car converted accommodation connected to church

indicators.note: converted means changed into another form, so the letters of the first three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone hands over a car that has been turned into living quarters for a parish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converted' rearranges GIVEACAR; the surface makes it sound like a garage conversion.
explanation.definitionFit: A vicarage is the house provided for a parish vicar, so it is lodging tied to a church.

clue.text: Increase journalist's investment in foreign currency

indicators.note: investment in reads as the journalist being put inside the currency, an insertion

parts.note: the rouble is the currency of Russia
ED, short for editor, stands for a journalist in crosswords

explanation.surface: A reporter puts more money into roubles or some other foreign currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'investment in' reads like finance, matching the currency, but it signals a container; ED for a journalist is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: To redouble is to make greater or intensify, as in redoubling one's efforts.

clue.text: Stacks fruit in cart out East

parts.note: ricks are stacks of hay or straw
a haw is the red fruit of the hawthorn

explanation.surface: Someone piles up fruit in a cart somewhere in the Orient.
explanation.definitionFit: A rickshaw is a light two-wheeled passenger vehicle pulled by a person, typical of East Asia.

clue.text: Course of treatment many soldiers fail to finish

indicators.note: fail to finish says the word for the soldiers stops short of its last letter

parts.note: a regiment is a large unit of soldiers

explanation.surface: A medical regime that a lot of troops do not complete.
explanation.definitionFit: A regimen is a prescribed plan of diet, exercise or medication.

clue.text: Have a drink — it evokes memories

parts.note: to keep something is to have or hold on to it
sake is Japanese rice wine

explanation.surface: An invitation to drink, as the drink brings back old memories.
explanation.definitionFit: A keepsake is a small item kept in remembrance of a person or event.

clue.text: Can hide a revolutionary in large estate

indicators.note: revolutionary suggests turning over and overthrowing, so the letters of the words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rebel fugitive may conceal themselves on a big ranch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' looks like a noun for the person being hidden, but it signals rearranging CANHIDEA.
explanation.definitionFit: A hacienda is a big landed estate or ranch in Spanish-speaking countries.

clue.text: Spoilsport producing fire extinguisher

explanation.surface: A killjoy said to be the source of something that puts out fires.
explanation.walkthrough: 'producing' is a link; a damp blanket thrown over flames smothers them, giving the literal sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who dampens others' fun is called this, and a soaked cover literally smothers a fire.

clue.text: Body monitoring two things private investigators do

parts.note: detectives watch their suspects, keeping them under observation
detectives also dog suspects, following them closely

explanation.surface: An organisation that oversees others, likened to the activities of private eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: A watchdog is an official body that monitors an industry or public sector for misconduct.

clue.text: Verse delivered in church office ahead of time

indicators.note: ahead of places the service's word before the letter for time

parts.note: terce is one of the canonical hours, a daily church service said at the third hour

explanation.surface: A poem is recited at a church service before the appointed time.
explanation.definitionFit: A tercet is a group of three lines of poetry, a short stanza.

clue.text: Make mistake with letters from Dickensian attorney's daughter?

parts.note: Miss is the title of an unmarried young woman, such as a daughter
Solomon Pell is the attorney in Dickens's The Pickwick Papers

explanation.surface: A question about what the daughter of a lawyer in Dickens would be called.
explanation.walkthrough: The daughter of Mr Pell would be Miss Pell; read as one word it means to spell wrongly.
explanation.definitionFit: To misspell is to write a word with the wrong letters.

clue.text: As an introduction, engage initially in quiet walk

parts.note: P, for piano, is the musical direction for quiet

indicators.note: in places the opening letter of engage inside the walk

parts.note: a ramble is a leisurely walk

indicators.note: initially means take only the first letter of the word engage

explanation.surface: To start, someone gets involved in a quiet stroll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As an' is a link; 'in' puts E inside RAMBLE after its R, with P in front.
explanation.definitionFit: A preamble is an opening statement that comes before the main body of a text or speech.

clue.text: Imagine that! No head, or covering for it

parts.note: to picture something is to imagine it

indicators.note: No head says the word that loses its first letter

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise about something without a head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' refers back to the head just mentioned, so the definition is a covering for a head.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture hat is a wide-brimmed decorated woman's hat, so it is headwear.

clue.text: Primitive people mass after victory in French city

indicators.note: in places the victory and mass letters inside the city

parts.note: Caen is a city in Normandy

indicators.note: after places the mass letter following the victory letters

parts.note: VE stands for Victory in Europe, as in VE Day
M is the symbol for mass in physics

explanation.surface: Ancient people gathered in a French city after a triumph.
explanation.walkthrough: VE Day was Victory in Europe Day, 8 May 1945, so 'victory' can give two letters; 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Cavemen were prehistoric people who lived in caves, a byword for primitive humans.

clue.text: Wandering around African republic, old volunteer nurse

indicators.note: around says the nurse's letters are placed round the country's name

parts.note: a VAD was a member of the Voluntary Aid Detachment, nursing volunteers of the World Wars
Gabon is a republic in west central Africa

explanation.surface: An elderly volunteer nurse roams around a country in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: The VAD nurses served in British hospitals during both World Wars; 'around' is the container signal, wrapping the nurse round the republic.
explanation.definitionFit: Vagabond as an adjective describes someone roaming from place to place with no fixed home.

clue.text: Travel over snow with space to spread out rapidly

parts.note: to mush is to travel by dog sled across snow
room means space, as in room to move

explanation.surface: A sled journey with plenty of space to fan out quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: To mushroom is to grow or expand very quickly, like the fungus springing up overnight.

clue.text: Treatment for bruising from hard, cold surface

explanation.surface: Help for a bruise gained by falling on a frozen surface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a link; the second sense reads the answer's words in reverse order, as pack ice, a frozen sheet on the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A bag of crushed ice applied to reduce swelling, and an expanse of drifting sea ice, both go by this name.

clue.text: Gradually propping up business in convincing fashion

indicators.note: in a down answer, propping up puts the second word beneath the first, supporting it

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a business
gently means gradually, as in a gently sloping road

explanation.surface: Slowly shoring up a company in a persuasive way.
explanation.definitionFit: Cogently means persuasively, with clear and forceful argument.

clue.text: Anteater inflicting pain on crippled lion

parts.note: a pang is a sudden sharp pain

indicators.note: crippled means damaged out of shape, so the letters of lion are rearranged

explanation.surface: An ant-eating animal hurts a lame lion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crippled' looks like part of a grim picture of animals, but it is the anagram signal for the big cat's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The pangolin is a scaly mammal that feeds on ants and termites.

clue.text: Record of survey that includes old island of ours

indicators.note: that includes says the survey word holds the other letters

parts.note: to survey is to look over, so look serves as the noun survey
GB, Great Britain, is the home island of a British newspaper's readers

explanation.surface: A record of a survey covering an ancient British island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'island of ours' is GB because The Times is a British paper; 'that includes' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A logbook is an official written record, such as a ship's daily journal.

clue.text: Keyboard operator given terrible roasting

indicators.note: terrible suggests something badly wrong, so the letters of roasting are rearranged

explanation.surface: A typist gets a fierce telling-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keyboard operator' suggests a typist, but it is a church musician.
explanation.definitionFit: An organist plays the organ, whose manuals are keyboards.

clue.text: Depend on others for cake

explanation.surface: Relying on others for one's cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: To sponge is to live off others' generosity, and a sponge is a light airy cake.

clue.text: Concerned with painful arrival

definitions.note: the noun arrival is matched by the answer used as a verbal noun

parts.note: RE means concerning or about, as in business letters
aching means sore or painful

explanation.surface: Worried about getting somewhere in pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Reaching a place is getting there, the act of arriving.

clue.text: Who do you say brings bad luck?

definitions.note: the clue's question asks for a thing that brings bad luck, so the phrase stands for a noun

indicators.note: you say signals that the words before it are spoken and heard as another word

parts.note: the two question words spoken together

explanation.surface: A question about who is to blame for misfortune.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoodoo is a jinx, a person or thing thought to cause misfortune.

clue.text: Attack successfully at the front? No

definitions.text: Attack successfully at the front? No

parts.words: Attack successfully at the front? No
parts.note: beating an enemy not by a head-on assault but by going round the side of their line

explanation.surface: A question about winning a battle by frontal assault, answered in the negative.
explanation.definitionFit: To outflank is to get round the side of an enemy force and so gain an advantage.

clue.text: It goes around nameless country — it shows where the sea was

definitions.text: it shows where the sea was

indicators.note: goes around says the word It turns about and is read backwards
nameless says N, the abbreviation for name, is removed from the country

parts.note: Denmark is a Scandinavian country

explanation.surface: Something circles an unnamed nation, marking where the sea once reached.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes around' is a reversal of the first word, not a container; 'nameless' drops N, the abbreviation for name, from the country.
explanation.definitionFit: A tidemark is the line left on a shore at the high-water level.

clue.text: American unknown to radio operator

explanation.surface: A US citizen whom a wireless operator has never heard of.
explanation.walkthrough: Y is the algebraic unknown, and in the radio alphabet Y is said as this word.
explanation.definitionFit: A Yankee is an informal name for an American, and it is the NATO phonetic code word for the letter Y.
